documentation.title: Coulomb friction under slidingType="large"
documentation.description:
Coulomb friction together with slidingType="large".
A block on a wider flat substrate, pressed by 1e6 Pa on its flat top and dragged sideways AT THE INTERFACE (prescribing the drag on the top face would put it a block height above the interface, and the resulting couple would lift one side off). Only u_x is prescribed, so the vertical support is still the contact interface.
WHAT IT ASSERTS
1. contactForceY = 1e6, the vertical equilibrium of the block. 2. totalTangentialForce = 4e5 = mu * F_N, all 24 points slipping, none sticking. The invariant is really the RATIO: it holds pointwise at every slipping point, so it holds for the resultant whatever the pressure distribution does. That matters, because a flat punch on an elastic half space has an edge singularity -- asserting a distribution would assert the mesh. 3. numContactElements 12 -> 14. An assembler element is one (secondary, primary) PAIR, so this integer changing is exactly the statement that points slid onto primary elements they were not paired with at the start. Under slidingType="small" it cannot change.
WHY normalPenalty IS 10 AND NOT THE SUITE'S USUAL 100. Friction under large sliding is limited by the product mu * normalPenalty -- the same product that limits tangent="consistent". Beyond it the failure is a runaway penetration, the normal direction blowing up and taking the friction force with it, and it is governed by that product rather than by how far the block slid. Keeping it small is what lets this model slide far enough for points to re-pair at all. A low penalty costs penetration; formulation="augmentedLagrange" removes that without raising it.
